newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-French unemployment in September.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-French unemployment in September.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on a 27,700 rise in French unemployment in September and an unemployment rate at a record 12.6 percent, reported by the labour ministry on Thursday.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast on average an increase of 15,000 in September.
SEAN SHEPLEY, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON
"They were clearly another poor set of labour market data at a time when we're seeing some signs of orders picking up in the manufacturing sector.
"The extent of the weakness will be worrying for the government and will add to the political pressure on them.

"It's a reminder of the weakness of domestic demand so that even though external orders may be picking up quite well...it will feed into low consumer confidence. It looks like we're heading for a pretty lousy fourth quarter."
VALERIE PLAGNOL, ECONOMIST, CREDIT COMMERCIAL DE FRANCE:

"It's really crystal clear, this is really bad. The worry is that there's a risk of still further deterioration. We are moving in parallel with Germany (on unemployment). It's bad for fourth quarter consumption."
JEAN-LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FINANCE:

"We were banking on unemployment rising to the end of the year but 0.9 percent is pretty big. Even if there are signs of an embryonic recovery it's not enough to help on unemployment. Fourth quarter growth is going to stay pretty weak".
JOANNE PEREZ, FRENCH STRATEGIST, MERRILL LYNCH
"I think in order for this to pass the Bank of France will have to cut rates as a sweetener, it's bad enough for a cut.

"What's interesting is that we've had a big pick-up in part-time employment in recent months. The unemployed plus the under-unemployed is something more like 3.23 million which puts the rate nearer to 13 percent.
"It suggests the consumer side of the economy is going to remain weak for some time."
